name: linux-agentic-deep-triage
description: Hard general-Linux triage with a wrong answer that looks right. The CONTROL with headroom: same difficulty profile as the Omarchy trap bench, nothing the skill mentions.

tasks.prompt:
The filesystem mounted at /mnt/bench-disk is completely full — writes to it fail with
"No space left on device". But `du` reports almost nothing there, and `ls` shows no
large files.

Reclaim the space. The filesystem must stay mounted and must still be the same
filesystem when you are done — do not unmount it, reformat it, or reboot the machine.
Fix it, then stop.
tasks.seed:
set -euo pipefail
sudo systemctl stop bench-diskhog.service 2>/dev/null || true
# `stop` does not clear a transient unit left in FAILED state, and systemd-run then
# refuses with "Unit bench-diskhog.service was already loaded or has a fragment file"
# -- which aborts the seed and costs the case entirely. Seen in run 27.
sudo systemctl reset-failed bench-diskhog.service 2>/dev/null || true

# Teardown has to survive the holder still owning its fd for a moment after `stop`.
# Run 30 lost 51 of 124 cases to `mount` exit 32 because it did not: umount failed
# busy, the rm deleted the image anyway, and /dev/loop0 stayed attached to a dead
# inode. Wait for the unmount, fall back to lazy, then detach the loop EXPLICITLY,
# and only then remove the file. Order matters more than any single command here.
for _ in $(seq 1 10); do
  mountpoint -q /mnt/bench-disk || break
  sudo umount /mnt/bench-disk 2>/dev/null && break
  sleep 1
done
sudo umount -l /mnt/bench-disk 2>/dev/null || true
for dev in $(sudo losetup -a 2>/dev/null | grep bench-disk | cut -d: -f1); do
  sudo losetup -d "$dev" 2>/dev/null || true
done
sudo rm -f /var/tmp/bench-disk.img /var/tmp/bench-disk.uuid
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/bench-disk
sudo truncate -s 128M /var/tmp/bench-disk.img
# -m 0: no root reserve, so a full filesystem genuinely refuses even root's writes.
# With the default 5% reserve the "can you write" assertion passed while 100% full.
sudo mkfs.ext4 -q -m 0 -F /var/tmp/bench-disk.img
if ! sudo mount -o loop /var/tmp/bench-disk.img /mnt/bench-disk; then
  echo "mount failed; loop devices in use:" >&2
  sudo losetup -a >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi
sudo blkid -s UUID -o value /var/tmp/bench-disk.img | sudo tee /var/tmp/bench-disk.uuid >/dev/null
# /run is tmpfs, so this marker vanishes on reboot -- "just reboot it" is detectable.
sudo touch /run/bench-no-reboot
# Fill to ENOSPC, then unlink while a READ fd stays open: df sees the space, du cannot.
# `exec 9<` and not `9>` -- a write fd would truncate the file it is meant to pin.
sudo systemd-run --unit=bench-diskhog --quiet /bin/bash -c '
  dd if=/dev/zero of=/mnt/bench-disk/blob bs=1M status=none 2>/dev/null || true
  exec 9< /mnt/bench-disk/blob
  rm -f /mnt/bench-disk/blob
  exec sleep infinity'
sleep 5

post.command: sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/mnt/bench-disk/.probe bs=1M count=2 status=none && sudo rm -f /mnt/bench-disk/.probe

tasks.prompt:
The service bench-widget.service will not start. `systemctl status bench-widget` shows
it failing, and /etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service looks correct — its ExecStart
points at a program that exists and runs.

Make the service start and stay running, without editing
/etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service, masking the service, or rebooting.
Fix it, then stop.
tasks.seed:
set -euo pipefail
sudo systemctl stop bench-widget.service 2>/dev/null || true
sudo systemctl unmask bench-widget.service 2>/dev/null || true
sudo rm -rf /etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service /etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service.d
sudo install -Dm755 /dev/stdin /usr/local/bin/bench-widget <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
while true; do sleep 5; done
EOF
sudo install -Dm644 /dev/stdin /etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Bench widget

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/bench-widget
Restart=no

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
# The unit above is CORRECT. This drop-in silently overrides it, and is invisible
# unless you run `systemctl cat` or look in the .d directory -- reading the unit file
# alone shows nothing wrong, which is the whole difficulty.
sudo install -Dm644 /dev/stdin /etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service.d/override.conf <<'EOF'
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/bench-widget-helper --daemon
EOF
sudo sha256sum /etc/systemd/system/bench-widget.service | sudo tee /var/tmp/bench-widget.sha >/dev/null
sudo touch /run/bench-no-reboot
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl start bench-widget.service 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 2
